findings.title: Local cache is set before the DB write, so a rejected device bypasses the limit afterward
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` calls `a.localCache.SetDefault(key, ...)` before `CreateOrUpdateDevice`. When the device limit is reached, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and the first request is rejected. The cache key is already set, so for the next ~29 minutes every request from that device hits the early `return nil` and is admitted anonymously without any DB record. The limit is therefore enforced only once per device per cache TTL. The cache entry should be set only after a successful write, or removed when the write fails.

findings.title: Limit check is a non-atomic count-then-insert, so concurrent requests can exceed the limit
findings.body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs `CountDevices` in one session and then does the upsert in another, with no transaction or lock. Concurrent requests from many new devices (and multiple Grafana instances) can all see `count < limit` and all insert, so the configured limit can be overshot. An insert guarded by the count (for example `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < ?`) or a transaction would make it enforceable. At the least the limit should be documented as best-effort.

findings.title: Device tagging moved from a background goroutine to the synchronous auth path
findings.body: The anonymous device tag used to run in a goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout and panic recovery. It now runs inline in `Authenticate` with the request context. Every anonymous request from a device not in the local cache now waits on a COUNT query plus an upsert (or update) before authentication completes. A slow or locked DB therefore adds latency to, or fails, anonymous requests. The panic recovery was also dropped. When the limit is not enabled there is no need to make this synchronous.

findings.title: Limit error returned raw from Authenticate with no user-facing handling or test
findings.body: When the limit is reached, `Authenticate` returns the bare `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. It is not wrapped as an authn error with a meaningful status or message, so the client likely sees a generic 401 or 500 and the server logs may be noisy. There are no tests for this client path or for `TagDevice` propagating the error, and the only new test is at the store level.

findings.title: Provider signature changed to take db.DB, which may break DI wiring
findings.body: `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` now takes `db.DB` and builds the store itself. `ProvideAnonDBStore` also now requires an `int64`, which wire cannot inject. If the wire set still binds `ProvideAnonDBStore`/`AnonStore`, wire generation or compilation fails. The diff shows no wire.go/wire_gen.go changes. Also, no `device_limit` entry was added to defaults.ini/sample.ini or the docs, so the new setting is undiscoverable.

findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit typed as undefined but backend always sends a number
findings.body: The backend DTO sends `anonymousDeviceLimit` as a non-omitempty int64, so it is `0` when unconfigured. The TS side declares `number | undefined` and defaults the field to `undefined`; the class field then infers type `undefined`. The type does not match the payload, and consumers must treat `0` as unlimited, which is not documented.
